title: Does This Value Work? Substitution as a Test
preview: An equation is a claim. Substitution is the test. Walk through values that work, values that don't, inequalities, two-solution cases, and stacked-fraction equations.

body.goal: Students see substitution as the *test* for whether a value satisfies an equation or inequality — not just the prelude to solving. They notice that some equations have two solutions, others have none, and inequalities can have many.
body.launch: Run the warm-up so the arithmetic is hot. Then start the slice. Don't ask kids to *solve* anything in this slice — only to check.
body.prerequisiteLabel: Warm up by evaluating small expressions — the inside of every check we'll do.

steps.teacherNote: Evaluates to 9. Confirms 'one specific value works'.
Diamond: TWO solutions exist. (-3)² = 9 ✓ as well. Substitution finds both.

steps.problem: Does x = 3 satisfy x + y = 7 when y = 4?
steps.teacherNote: Two variables. Both slots filled to test. 3 + 4 = 7 ✓.

enrichmentSteps.teacherNote: Only x = 3 (= 9 - 3 = 6). x = -2 also works algebraically but isn't in the set.
Diamond: two solutions in the set. Both work.
Inequality — multiple values work. x = 2 gives 5 < 5 (false).

body.consolidation: Bring them back. 'On step 11, x = -3 also worked. So x² = 9 has *two* solutions. Does every equation have one solution?' (No — and this is foundational for grade 8.) 'On the inequality steps (5, 6, and enrichment 4), more than one value works. What's different about inequalities?' (They describe a *range*, not a point.)
